title: Ad-hoc export preview with cost estimation and throttled S3 staging
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Customers frequently open ad-hoc usage exports from the Console to inspect recent token usage, billing-relevant spikes, or to validate filters before scheduling a full export. Today the 'Export Now' flow immediately enqueues a full export job which can take hours and incur unanticipated egress / S3 costs for large tenants.

Goal:
Implement an interactive ad-hoc export preview + dry-run that returns (1) a sample CSV preview (first N rows + representative sampling) stored as a short-lived signed URL, (2) an estimated export size and approximate S3 cost and transfer time, and (3) an option to stage the full export into S3 using a throttled writer that respects tenant-priority and cluster throughput so we don't spike downstream egress or affect production serving.

Key requirements / acceptance criteria:
- Console: "Preview export" button returns a preview signed URL within 10s for small queries and 30s for complex queries.
- Cost estimate: Provide a transparent estimate (MB, token-count proxy, estimated $ S3 egress) with +/-25% accuracy for >100MB outputs. Estimate must explain assumptions (sample rate, avg row size).
- Throttled staging: When user selects "Stage full export", backend writes to S3 using tenant-aware throttling and backpressure so that sustained export throughput does not exceed configured tenant quota or cluster egress budget.
- Failure modes: If staging falls behind or S3 write fails, user sees clear status and resumable retry option. Exports must be idempotent and support resume from last successful chunk.
- Observability: Track preview latency, estimate accuracy (compare estimate vs actual size), staging throughput per tenant, and tenant-throttle incidents.
- Cost control: Allow finance-only admins to set export throughput caps and auto-fail staging if projected monthly egress exceeds tenant budget.

Design notes / proposed approach:
1) Query sampling: Reuse the existing export query planner to execute a bounded sampler (LIMIT + stratified sampling across time windows) to approximate row count and row size distribution. Store sampler output in ephemeral Redis cache (TTL 10m).
2) Preview artifact: Generate a preview CSV (up to 500 rows) and upload to a short-lived S3 prefix with lifecycle TTL 24h. Return signed GET URL to Console.
3) Cost estimator: Use query planner outputs + model of average row tokenization to compute estimated tokens -> bytes -> S3 MB. Apply region pricing table from pricing-service to project $ egress. Store estimator version in export_job metadata for future reconciliation.
4) Throttled staging worker: New export-worker mode that accepts target throughput (bytes/s or rows/s) per job. Worker periodically consults tenant-quota service and global export budget service to compute per-job rate and uses adaptive sleep + small upload parts (5MB chunks) to S3 to maintain throttle. Support chunk checkpointing (manifest of uploaded parts) for resumability.
5) API changes: Add POST /v1/exports/dry-run that returns preview_url, estimate, sampler_id. Add POST /v1/exports/stage referencing sampler_id and throttle_policy.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (internal alpha): Implement sampler + preview CSV + estimator behind feature flag. Enable for internal Redwood orgs and 3 pilot customers. Collect accuracy metrics. (2 weeks)
- Phase 2 (beta): Implement throttled staging worker and resume semantics. Enable opt-in via console for paid tenants. (3 weeks)
- Phase 3 (GA): Expose caps in finance settings, enable default small-tenant caps, and flip feature flag cluster-wide. (1 week)

Monitoring & SLOs:
- Preview latency P95 < 30s; alert if >5% of previews exceed SLA for 24h.
- Estimation error median <15%, 95th <40% after phase 1 tuning.
- Staging worker error rate <1% and resume success rate >99%.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for sampler correctness and estimator math (edge cases: compressed CSVs, unusual row sizes).
- Integration tests with a local minio S3 and mocked pricing-service to validate estimate -> actual reconciliation.
- Load tests to validate throttled staging under contended cluster conditions (simulate many concurrent large exports).

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Sampling strategy: stratified time buckets vs reservoir sampling. Reservoir is simpler but can miss distributional shifts. Need perf run to decide.
- Where to persist estimator version: job metadata vs manifest blob. Prefer job metadata for ease of reconciliation.
- Throttle enforcement point: worker-level only vs central scheduler. Worker-level is easier to start with but central scheduler gives stronger global guarantees.

Acceptance demo:
- From Console, run "Preview export" on a 30-day tenant dataset -> show preview URL, cost estimate, and sample CSV.
- Trigger "Stage full export" -> show staged S3 object appearing under tenant-staged prefix and Console status with throughput graph.
- Simulate S3 error and show resume flow.

Migration / cleanup:
- Add background job to sweep preview prefixes older than 24h.
- Backfill estimator versions for existing export jobs created in 2026 using a reconciliation job (best-effort).
